hypothesis: Product-tree residue epochs improve projective-probe throughput by at least 2x including isolation and memory cost.
baselines: one batched GCD per projective comparison
primary_metric: frozen residues processed per CPU-second under peak-memory cap
result: Median paired throughput 1.409x (epoch 256), 1.409x (1024), 1.401x (4096), below the preregistered 2x gate; exact factor yield preserved and masking isolation passed.
next_action: retain moderate epochs only as a profiled constant-factor option; proceed to held-out AQ-010 predictor study

hypothesis: Public auxiliary-prime orbit features predict held-out factor yield beyond size, seed count, and feature cost.
primary_metric: held-out paired end-to-end yield per CPU-second
result: Held-out auxiliary model worsened log loss (0.1696 vs 0.1569) and AUC (0.9677 vs 0.9734); top-3 scheduling split 4/20 integers versus 6/20 random, with paired bootstrap interval [-0.25, 0.00] and lower end-to-end yield.
next_action: do not promote this feature family; proceed to size/root-score-matched SR-011 smooth-relation study

hypothesis: Short-word orbit norms improve unique usable smooth-relation yield after matching norm size and root score.
primary_metric: unique usable relations per total CPU-second
result: At B=1000 over 60 balanced semiprimes and 30,720 observations per arm, Berggren proposals yielded 852 smooth relations versus 856 matched controls; Fibonacci/Lucas proposals yielded 1,230 versus 1,219. Paired 95% bootstrap intervals for rate differences both crossed zero.
next_action: do not promote scalar structured offsets; test periodic-word order families and one/two-large-prime relation completion

hypothesis: Cheap structural fingerprints improve rho/ECM allocation tail latency on a frozen mixed corpus.
primary_metric: median and 90th-percentile time to certified split

hypothesis: A frozen algebraically diverse panel of periodic Berggren words exposes smooth projective orders not explained by p-1 or p+1.
primary_metric: held-out certified splits per counted scalar modular multiplication
result: At B=1000 on 60 balanced semiprimes, Berggren words split 41 cases versus 17 multiplicative and 29 Lucas-torus; 12 splits were outside the union of both controls. But yield was only 1.31 splits per million counted modular multiplications versus 10.31 and 2.63, respectively.
next_action: do not promote the 3x3 implementation; reduce words to deduplicated second-order Lucas/Chebyshev recurrences and retest against production p-1, Williams p+1, and ECM on held-out larger inputs

hypothesis: Structured offsets improve completed one/two-large-prime relation cycles despite no full-smoothness advantage.
primary_metric: independent completed relations per frozen relation pool; end-to-end timing deferred unless pool-quality gate passes
result: At large-prime bound 1000000, Berggren produced 972 completed relations versus 993 control and Fibonacci/Lucas 1462 versus 1450 control. Paired 95% bootstrap intervals [-1.467, 0.817] and [-1.217, 1.667] both crossed zero; partial-cycle counts were 120/137 and 232/231.
next_action: do not promote scalar structured offsets; proceed to periodic-word orders or jointly matched Gaussian two-norm relations
